title: CONTROL Resonant Artifacts: Slots, Crafting, and Confirmed Items
excerpt: How Artifacts modify builds, where Untapped Artifacts are shaped, which preorder items are named, and what NG+ changes.
introduction: Artifacts are passive build items with more variety than simple damage bonuses. Remedy says they can affect combat, survival, exploration, and resource economy, sometimes with activation conditions or tradeoffs.
quickAnswer: Players equip up to three Artifacts in the first playthrough and unlock a fourth slot in New Game Plus. Untapped Artifacts found during play are shaped in The Gap. Pickpocket's Tool and the Digital Deluxe Wallet are confirmed named bonuses, but their final effects have not been published on the store pages checked here.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden in The Gap, where Untapped Artifacts can be shaped

sections.title: How do Artifacts work in CONTROL Resonant?
paragraphs: The official NG+ article describes the system's roles and limits but does not publish a complete Artifact catalog. This guide names only items that appear in official edition listings.

rows: Passive support for staying alive or recovering from pressure
Modifiers that reinforce a chosen melee or ability setup
Effects connected to moving through or searching the world
Changes to how build resources are gained or spent
Bonuses that require a condition or impose a tradeoff
table.caption: What Artifact effects can change

sections.title: Untapped Artifacts and The Gap
paragraphs: Untapped Artifacts are discovered during play and taken into The Gap, the dreamlike buildcrafting space connected to Dylan. There they can be shaped into usable Artifacts.
This makes optional discovery part of progression. Remedy has not published the full shaping cost or outcome rules.

image.alt: The blue dreamlike buildcrafting realm called The Gap
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of The Gap.

sections.title: Confirmed named bonus items

rows: Not disclosed on the checked store pages
Must be shaped; final effect not disclosed
table.caption: Confirmed named bonus items

paragraphs: A suggestive name is not enough evidence for an effect. This site will not claim that Pickpocket's Tool changes drops, stealing, or currency unless the launch inventory says so.

sections.title: Three slots first, four in New Game Plus
paragraphs: Three slots force tradeoffs during the initial campaign. New Game Plus adds a fourth, enabling combinations unavailable in the first run while preserving collected Artifacts.
Artifacts carry into NG+, unlike story-gated traversal abilities.

sections.title: How to evaluate an Artifact
bullets: Read the trigger condition before comparing the headline bonus.
Check whether the effect supports melee, abilities, survival, exploration, or economy.
Account for any tradeoff instead of ranking by one number.
Test whether the effect remains active through Form switches and executions.
Revisit the setup when the fourth NG+ slot becomes available.

title: CONTROL Resonant Talents, Zone XP & Respec Guide
excerpt: How zone activities award Talent points, what the upgrade tree shows, the preview Respec All control, and additional NG+ progression.
introduction: Manhattan's zone progression and Dylan's Talent tree are connected. The August developer interview and the official interface now give us a clearer view of both systems.
quickAnswer: Activities award XP to zones rather than directly to Dylan. Each zone level grants a zone improvement and a Talent point, according to IGN's developer interview. Respec All is visible in the official preview interface; its final cost is not established by the screenshot.
imageAlt: CONTROL Resonant Talent tree with branching attack upgrades

sections.title: How does the Talent tree work?
paragraphs: The interface is pre-release and can receive visual, wording, cost, or balance changes before or after launch.

sections.title: How zone XP earns Talent points
paragraphs: IGN's August 19 developer interview describes zone-level rewards including better health drops, revealed loot chests and access to arcade challenge cabinets. Each zone level also gives a Talent point.
Defeating Resonants unlocks Combat Abilities and makes world encounters more dangerous. Clearing a boss does not simply remove a threat from a static map.

sections.title: Primary, Secondary, and Combo Enders
paragraphs: The three visible tabs mirror the Aberrant's combat structure. Primary and Secondary Forms determine major parts of the active moveset, while Combo Enders finish attack strings with specialized effects.
A branching tree supports different routes. It does not prove that every branch is mutually exclusive or that a choice is permanent.

image.alt: Talent menu showing Primary, Secondary, and Combo Enders tabs
image.caption: Official PlayStation Blog screenshot. Only clearly readable labels are treated as confirmed.

sections.title: Dodge Attack node
paragraphs: Dodge Attack is readable in the published screenshot. It modifies an attack immediately after a dodge, launching enemies and adding damage. Aberrant Strength is displayed, but the image alone does not establish a purchase cost or final rank requirement.

sections.title: Can you respec Talents?
paragraphs: The official screenshot visibly includes Respec All. That is evidence of a preview respec interface, not proof of a free, unlimited launch system. The control alone does not establish resource costs, refunds or when respec becomes available.

sections.title: Talents are one part of the loadout
paragraphs: Talents sit beside Weapon Forms, Combat Abilities, and Artifacts. A full build still needs an ability-power loop, a way to create Falter or control space, and passive support suited to the encounter.
That is why a final Talent tier list requires tested damage values and enemy behavior rather than icon placement alone.

sections.title: New Game Plus progression
paragraphs: Talents already unlocked carry over. NG+ adds new nodes, expands the Artifact limit from three to four, and allows additional Combat Ability choices from previously defeated Resonants.
Traversal abilities do not carry because they remain tied to story progression.

title: CONTROL Resonant World Quests and Exploration
excerpt: How Dylan's Journey, World Quests, zones, Gravity Anomalies, hidden encounters, traversal, and seamless dialogue fit together.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant is open-ended, but Remedy does not describe it as one uniform map filled with repeated tasks. Manhattan is built from large handcrafted zones with narrative and systemic reasons to leave the main route.
quickAnswer: Dylan's Journey is the main campaign, while World Quests are optional narrative stories inside Manhattan's zones. Exploration also reveals side activities, hidden encounters, environmental challenges, collectibles, and Gravity Anomalies. Zoe De Vera can provide seamless dialogue while Dylan moves through the world.
imageAlt: A Manhattan street with people and objects suspended by a Gravity Anomaly

sections.title: Quest and exploration structure
paragraphs: Remedy uses 'expansive' for the zones and 'open-ended' for the game. That supports exploration freedom without proving a seamless open world or a particular number of districts.

sections.title: Dylan's Journey
paragraphs: Dylan's Journey is the central campaign. Dylan leaves the Oldest House, enters the Manhattan crisis, searches for Jesse, and confronts the entity and resonance changing reality.
A full launch campaign order is not published. Named preview locations such as Metro Fault are indexed separately from verified retail mission routes.

image.alt: Dylan Faden overlooking the transformed city
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store art for Dylan's Manhattan journey.

sections.title: World Quests
paragraphs: World Quests are optional narrative stories discovered in the zones. Remedy distinguishes them from the main campaign and says the world contains characters, lore, secrets, and encounters with their own context.
The NG+ article says World Quests can be revisited and some choices can lead to changed outcomes or conversations. It does not claim that every quest has multiple endings.

sections.title: Large, distinct Manhattan zones
paragraphs: The West Incursion Zone is the first named Manhattan zone in Remedy's gameplay announcement. Other areas have distinct atmospheres, encounters, lore, side activities, and optional discoveries.
A zone-based structure allows traversal unlocks to reveal new routes without requiring every space to be available from the opening hour.

image.alt: An overhead view of a distorted Manhattan zone
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of the game's expansive city spaces.

sections.title: Gravity Anomalies
paragraphs: Gravity Anomalies are named spaces where gravity and orientation shift entirely. Official images show environments becoming vertical, inverted, or otherwise impossible to read like a normal street or corridor.
They function as traversal and environmental challenges, not merely as background decoration.

image.alt: A tall brutalist environment reoriented by a Gravity Anomaly
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of a vertical gravity-shifted space.

sections.title: Faults and the Metro Fault preview
paragraphs: IGN's August gameplay feature names Metro Fault, a dungeon-like location associated with the Reach movement unlock. It is a documented preview location, not a complete retail mission route.

links.label: Metro Fault and Reach preview guide
How zone XP rewards Talent points

sections.title: Traversal seen in a media demo
paragraphs: Game Informer's hands-on preview described a double jump, air dash, and a stronger jump that becomes a brief float. It also described optional surreal sequences involving a sinkhole, shifting apartments, and music moving between televisions.
Those are observations from a controlled preview build, not final mission names, a complete traversal list, or proof of where the events occur in the launch campaign.

sections.title: Zoe De Vera and seamless dialogue
paragraphs: Zoe De Vera is an FBC field agent assigned as Dylan's handler. Remedy says her conversations with Dylan can play seamlessly during exploration, giving context without repeatedly pulling the player into a separate cutscene.
This does not make Zoe a playable cooperative partner; CONTROL Resonant remains a single-player game.

image.alt: Zoe De Vera speaking with Dylan Faden
image.caption: Official PlayStation Store screenshot of Dylan and his FBC handler.
